title: Sector mobility and formal union membership differ across US industries
source_unit: BLS JOLTS establishment rates and CPS union-affiliation industry estimates

quits_rate.unit: percent annual arithmetic mean of monthly rate

job_openings_rate.unit: percent annual arithmetic mean of monthly rate

observations.method: BLS JOLTS 2025 annual arithmetic mean of monthly seasonally adjusted establishment rates.
observations.uncertainty: JOLTS measures establishments and not unique workers; rates are revised and do not identify transition reasons or job quality.
observations.counterinterpretation: Mobility rates cannot be read as worker power or as outcomes caused by representation.

denominator.unit: thousand employed wage and salary workers in industry

observations.method: BLS CPS Union Members 2025 Table 3 annual average; membership is a descriptive institutional-representation measure.
observations.uncertainty: CPS survey and classification uncertainty apply; BLS states 2025 annual estimates exclude October and are not strictly comparable with prior annual averages.
observations.counterinterpretation: Membership does not measure practical schedule control, grievance success, autonomy, or the causal effect of a union on JOLTS mobility.

related_sources.claim: CPS industry union-membership estimates provide institutional context for selected JOLTS sectors.
related_sources.access_boundary: The two BLS programs use different populations, sampling frames, measures, and denominators; this is a conditioning comparison, not a joined worker dataset.

boundary: This record places 2025 sector-level establishment mobility beside CPS formal union membership. It does not estimate a causal representation effect, worker bargaining power, job quality, pay, schedule control, household security, or political meaning.
